task_name: Ridgeway Rovers - Football crest master system
client_brief:
Recover a football crest and its hand-drawn shirt lettering

Ridgeway Rovers wants its existing identity back in usable form. The crest needs to work at breast size and in one ink; the lettering comes from a set of 1990s drawings rather than a font we can buy.

Scope
1. Football club crest: 3 named exports. The club lettering matches the source. The crest details remain recognisable at shirt size.
2. Club number glyph: 10 named exports. The numeral is unambiguous at kit viewing distance. The glyph follows the founder's drawing.
3. Club letter glyph: 26 named exports. The letter follows the founder's drawing. The letter has no graph-paper artefacts.
4. Shirt and training-kit artwork sheet: 1 named export. The crest placement respects the supplied kit dimensions. The name-number hierarchy is usable on the shirt.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Grassroots amateur football club refreshing its playing kit, crest and shirt numbering through one local kit supplier.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1974, a village near Cirencester in the Cotswolds, with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups.
brand_identity.about: Ridgeway Rovers are a village football club that has worn the same crest since 1974 and drawn their own shirt numbering since the nineties. This season brings the first new shirt since 2019. The club wants its own crest and its own hand drawn numbering back as proper artwork, so any supplier can print it and it still looks like Ridgeway.
brand_identity.audience: Players and parents at twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt, often buying a child's fourth kit in five years, who want something that looks like a proper club.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Grassroots, twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt printed by one local supplier. Numbering has to reduce to a single robust cuttable colour for heat press and flock, honest rather than pro tier.
brand_identity.typography: The crest lettering is small caps set in a ring. The numbering is the club's own hand drawn alphabet and digits, rebuilt as even, solid, cuttable geometry. A supporting text face for the spec and boards sits behind the drawn work, never over it.
brand_identity.voice: Straightforward, warm, club room plain. Example line: Same crest we have worn since 1974, cleaned up so any printer can do it justice.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No artwork survives. The former kit secretary took the crest files when he moved away, leaving only a parent's phone photo of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. The numbering exists only as two marker on graph paper sheets, an alphabet and a digit set, drawn by a founding member in the nineties and photographed on a kitchen table. Last season's supplier back of shirt sheet is on hand as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping what is genuinely theirs, the 1974 crest and the founder's numbering, and reading as a real village club rather than a franchise or a school project.

Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
